docs/plan-speed-and-ir-s470.md Part B item B4.

=== DONE (s470bm) ===

SHIPPED
  tools/ir-host-leak.pl      the census; reads B1's docs/ir-op-inventory.tsv
                             for the runtime half, so the two Part-B
                             instruments share ONE list
  docs/ir-spec.md §11b       "The CL kernel a backend must implement" — the
                             100 measured names, grouped, each with its JS and
                             C rendering; the five READER rules a text-parsing
                             backend needs; and the leak table with its tasks
  Pl/t/ir-host-leak-01.t     11 rows, 924 ms

THE CLAIM: an emitted file contains only (i) runtime exports, (ii) the
whitelisted CL kernel, (iii) literals, (iv) the program's own identifiers.
Anything else is a leak.  Nothing else in the tree can see one — the gate runs
the CL on SBCL, where a host symbol works perfectly.

THE WHITELIST IS MEASURED, not enumerated from the standard: run with
`--unclassified`, classify what comes back by hand once, keep the closed set.
100 names.  That number is the size of a backend's host-side job, and
Pl/t/ir-host-leak-01.t asserts §11b's stated size equals the tool's set so the
two copies cannot drift.

THREE CLASSIFIER DECISIONS THAT WERE WRONG FIRST AND ARE MEASURED NOW:
  * POSITION matters.  `(block start …)`'s `start` is a perl LABEL and is the
    same SHAPE as a leaked CL function.  The scanner tracks four positions —
    op / quoted / bind / arg — and only the first two are claims about the
    host.  Without it the census reported 51 `_prev`, every `pcl-local-*` temp
    and every label as leaks.
  * A HEADLESS list's first element is a BINDING NAME, not an operator: a list
    whose own first element is a list (`((x 1))`) is headless, and that is
    exactly the shape of every binding list, lambda list and plist the emitter
    writes.  This is what took the compiler temps out.
  * A `pcl::`-qualified token is NOT a program identifier.  Treating it as one
    (it looks package-qualified) hid a whole class — see #1177.

THE MEASUREMENT
  perl-tests   111 files, 175,317 tokens   38 distinct leaked symbols
  lib/**.pm     22 files, module mode      only `use integer`'s
  perl's t/    592 files, 522,620 tokens   the same set + two REAL BUGS the
                                           census found and nothing else had:
                                           #1178 (`p-my`, a non-existent op
                                           that kills the file) and #1179
                                           (`-norequire` becomes a superclass)

FILED, NOT FIXED (B4's brief): #1175 the CL-function families, #1176 the
quoted-symbol ambiguity, #1177 the five qualified internals, #1178, #1179.

WHAT TO RUN WHEN — for Fable to add to CLAUDE.md's table (this agent may not
edit that file): the population census belongs on the `cl/**` row and on the
`Pl/**`-with-diffs row.  `tools/ir-host-leak.pl` (~40 s over 111 files) after
a change that adds or renames an export, or that changes what the emitter can
put in the output.  The recipe is in the tool's header and in §11b; the gate
row covers only the known families' fixtures.
